decisions.mark: states that by default the macro RENAMES the member to private_<member>, and that defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS makes it expand to the member name unchanged
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Without `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS`, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)` expands to `private_foo`. ... With the define, it expands to `foo` and the name is visible again. | WHY: The answer states both the default rename to private_<member> and the unchanged expansion when MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS is defined.

decisions.mark: explains that the two branches give different consumers different views — code that defines MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS sees plain member names while an ordinary consumer of the public headers sees the renamed ones
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Without `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS`, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)` expands to `private_foo`. The struct declares the field as `private_foo`, so application code that writes `ctx->foo` fails to compile... With the define, it expands to `foo` and the name is visible again. | WHY: The answer states that code defining the macro sees plain names while ordinary application consumers see the renamed `private_` members. || QUOTE: "Without `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS`, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)` expands to `private_foo`... so application code that writes `ctx->foo` fails to compile... With the define, it expands to `foo`" and "Applications are the ones who get the rename." | WHY: The answer contrasts code that defines the macro, which sees plain names, with ordinary application consumers, who see the `private_` renamed members.

decisions.mark: concludes that this enforces API opacity at COMPILE time by breaking the member name, rather than by hiding the struct layout — the fields remain visible and sized
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Without `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS`, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)` expands to `private_foo`. The struct declares the field as `private_foo`, so application code that writes `ctx->foo` fails to compile with "no member named foo"." | WHY: The answer explains the compile-time rename mechanism but never states that the struct layout stays visible and sized, nor contrasts this with hiding the layout (opaque types). || QUOTE: "Without `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS`, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)` expands to `private_foo`. The struct declares the field as `private_foo`, so application code that writes `ctx->foo` fails to compile with "no member named foo"." | WHY: The answer explains the compile-time rename, but never states that the struct layout stays visible and sized, so it does not contrast the rename with hiding the layout.
